## Authority contract

Only the existing `pgAgentJournal()` default factory can register a native journal. Its private registry binds the actual client, original class prototype and own descriptors. It checks every captured method descriptor, the client target and scalar parser/serializer provenance, synchronous client close state and the current default selector. A copied journal, tooling constructor, changed method/accessor, substituted prototype, foreign target or replaced cache cannot register authority. Legitimate `ready()` transitions update only the privately captured readiness state after validating its old state. A substituted readiness promise or getter cannot rebrand the object. The exported predicates and tuple reader cannot register a caller object or grant writes.

The application `agentJournal()` selector reads its own global descriptor before and after the existing lazy PostgreSQL import. It refuses accessor or concurrent foreign selection without invoking getters or setters. Journal selection uses the same product store selector; capability/schema authorization remains at the existing entry points and journal methods. The default client selector is descriptor-checked before construction. Legacy file and structural read/test behavior retain their existing API; those objects cannot populate the private native OAuth dispatch maps. Historical cached objects without this factory's private membership need a fresh trusted process before native mutation admission.

The current integration resolver first asks the genuine native linked credential authority whether the global integration ID exists. A known linked identity, including a revoked, expired, foreign-workspace or OAuth-shaped collision, cannot fall back to OAuth. The dedicated native OAuth read repeats global linked-ID absence and selects only the eleven nonsecret columns from `agent.agent_oauth_grants`: integration ID, subject, client ID, workspace, issuer, expiry, revocation, projects, environments, apps and scopes. It requires canonical journal migration versions 1, 2 and 3, bounded native types, exact subject/workspace and configured issuer. It never selects token hashes, tokens, keys, arbitrary documents or provider secrets.

The resolver freezes that tuple and binds it to the exact principal object, actual default journal and linked authority, current selector and exact validated OAuth configuration. Copies and caller-supplied scopes cannot produce this binding. The canonical worker evaluator captures this genuine result before approving-human awaits. Its private current dispatch requirement requires exactly one linked credential or OAuth origin, exact evaluated access, current project/environment coverage and the correct capability scope. A delegated source-free destroy still requires its genuine system teardown-review binding, current planning grant and exact current human administrator approvals. An ordinary integration mutation still requires the current editor/admin member and write scope.

After the actual artifact use-row wait, the existing repository calls the genuine requirement lookup and repeats current journal/client/owner/selector/configuration provenance after any policy await. It issues no authority-pool query inside the occupied owning transaction. The final fresh READ COMMITTED statement compares the complete OAuth tuple, rejects any global linked credential collision, requires current unrevoked/unexpired scope coverage, and repeats existing current product/source/recipe/provider/lease/requester/consumed-approver/policy/settings/evidence predicates. The grant row belongs to the same proved opening target as the native owner. Separate stores are refused; a matching environment URL alone is insufficient.

Nullable and empty app metadata are compared exactly. A change from `[]` to null is an authority tuple change. Nonempty app metadata, resource-scoped product requests, Navigator/file/separate targets and unavailable native authority remain refused until their own bounded support exists. This packet does not add that support or reduce the product's requirements.

Accepted or uncertain provider calls retain the existing original attempt and non-replay behavior. Final admission cannot retract an accepted provider call. It establishes current admission at the native statement boundary, without asserting a distributed atomic transaction with OAuth token verification, the external issuer or later cloud effects.
